Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 51, English)
The Space Element ( आ क ाश त त्व ): Redefining What "God" Actually Is

Sour ce: an extended, highly Socratic Mool T atva live session in which Bhaiya cr owd-sour ces the sangat's own definitions of God/divinity , systematically tests each answer , and arrives at a working definition gr ounded in the five classical elements — culminating in practical guidance on jaap, bhakti, and an upcoming Dhanteras hawan.
1. The Opening Question: "What Is God?"

Bhaiya opens by directly asking the assembled sangat (roughly 200 people) to define God. A wide range of answers come in rapid succession: param tatva (the supreme element), that which is all-pervading and present within everything, a source of ener gy , the "purest form," soul, the five elements combined (bhoomi/gagan/vayu — earth/sky/air), supreme consciousness, "brahmand ki sarvochya shakti" (the universe's supreme power), "aham brahmasmi," an entity reached where physics and mathematics fail to draw conclusions, parmanand (supreme bliss), and more.
2. Testing Each Answer for Internal Contradiction

Rather than accepting any single answer , Bhaiya methodically points out the logical tension in several: if the universe's "supreme power" is God, what then is the rest of the universe? If everything is God — "aham brahmasmi," where surrender itself is God — does that mean an unfortunate accident is also God's direct doing? He deliberately stress-tests each of fered definition rather than settling for it, to show that most common definitions of God are either too vague or self-contradictory when examined closely .
3. A Note on Continuity With Earlier Teaching

One sangat member recalls that an earlier Mool Tatva video had linked God to one's own "inner consciousness" or intuition (the voice that tells you right from wrong), and had connected this to the Kuldevi concept discussed in a separate session. Bhaiya acknowledges the earlier teaching but is explicit that today's concept is a distinctly differ ent framework , not a restatement of the earlier one.
4. The Five Elements, and Which Ones We Can Actually Per ceive

Bhaiya grounds the discussion in the five classical elements (panchtatva): earth, water , fire, air , and space (aakash) . He walks through each: earth, water , fire, and air can all be directly seen or felt — air , for instance, can be felt when it moves things (a storm), or when mixed into water (pressure) or into earth (soil); fire can be felt as heat; all four of these elements are perceivable through direct sensation or through mixing with another element.
5. The One Element You Can Never See or Feel: Space

Of the five elements, only the space element (aakash tatva) can neither be seen nor felt — yet it undeniably exists. Bhaiya clarifies this is not about outer -space astronomy (planets, stars) — it specifically means the fifth element the sages/saints (sant) describe as composing this earth, distinct from anything found "out there" in the literal cosmos.
6. The Cor e Definition: Space Element = God

Because the space element is the one thing on Earth that can never be seen or felt by ordinary human senses, yet still exists, Bhaiya defines it directly as God : "Har wo vastu jo insaan ko na dikhayi de sake, na sunayi de sake, na wo feel kar sake, wo Bhagwan hai" (Everything that a human being can neither see, hear , nor feel — yet which exists — is God).
7. How the Space Element "Divinizes" Whatever It Enters

Per this teaching, wherever the space element mixes into any other element or object, that object becomes divine. A murti (idol), a body , holy water , sacred food — whatever the space element enters becomes "bhagwan" in that specific sense. This is of fered as the underlying mechanism behind practices like holy water and consecrated food.
8. Why We Are Naturally Possessive About the Space Element

Bhaiya states plainly that regardless of how many Sanskrit shlokas one reads or how many alternative definitions are of fered, in practice people specifically tr eat only the space element as God — precisely because it is the one thing on Earth that cannot be seen or felt, making it uniquely sacred by elimination.
9. The Subtle Chakra System and Astral Connection

Within the body exists a subtle chakra system; when these chakras (referred to here as sookshm chakras) open, a person becomes connected to the astral world (paralaukik jagat). This teaching states that such a person is said to have a very active space element, which allows them to draw ener gies from the astral world — this is exactly why people touch such a person's feet, treating them as "related to God."
10. Paranormal Entities Also Fall Under This Framework

Even a bhoot or pret (ghost/spirit), while distinct from a human being, can perform actions a human cannot — and per this teaching, this alone is suf ficient for people to categorically place such an entity in the "God"/divine category , because it exhibits the same defining trait (unseen, unfelt by ordinary means, yet capable of action beyond human capacity).
1 1. Activating Your Own Space Element Means Touching God's Own Element

A crucial corollary follows directly from the definition: when any human being awakens the space element within their own body , they ar e literally awakening the element of God within themselves — not merely something God-like, but the actual same tatva.
12. Case Study: The Non-Devotional Army Colonel

To test whether devotion (bhakti) is strictly required to access this element, Bhaiya presents an extended case study: a soldier who never worships, doesn't consciously know or invoke God, gets selected out of lakhs of applicants for a competitive post, rises to Colonel, and enjoys a prosperous, obstacle-free family life. Since no murti puja, no devta worship, and no explicit invocation of Hanuman ji or Bhagwan Ram occurred, how is this possible?
13. Resolution: He "T ouched" Divinity Without Realizing It

Bhaiya's resolution: such a person did, in fact, touch the space element/divinity — just not through conscious devotional means. This teaching states the mechanism is "atha mehnat" (extreme, sustained ef fort): when a person performs any single activity with enough repetition over enough time, a saturation point is reached where the person becomes so completely submer ged in the activity that they move beyond their own ordinary awareness — muscle memory takes over , the subtle (astral) body activates, and that astral body in turn activates the space element.
14. "Activation of Space Element Cr eates Miracles"

Once this saturation point is hit even once ("vons you hit that"), per this teaching the space element does not fully deactivate afterward — the person retains an ongoing connection and will keep finding a "way forward" in that domain from then on. This is of fered as the reason people who work with obsessive intensity in any field (soldiers, scientists, architects) report sudden clarity or breakthrough "answers" after an extreme session of focused ef fort (e.g., a soldier's daily hour -long run pushing him into this activated state).
15. Devotion Is Not Requir ed — But It Is One Route

This teaching explicitly states devotion (bhakti) is not a strict requirement for activating the space element — the army Colonel example illustrates a non-devotional route. Bhakti is instead redefined as one particular technique/method for accessing the space element, alongside extreme secular ef fort in any domain.
16. Devi-Devata Shakti Defined Within This Framework

Devi-devata (deity) ener gies are described, within this framework, as powerful, already-activated ener gies belonging to the space element itself — accessible aids that can help a person enter or connect with the space element, and thus worthy of reverence and worship.
17. What Happens After Activation Belongs to Destiny/Dimension/Pitru Mechanisms

Once a person's space element is activated, this teaching states that what happens next — their prarabdh (destiny), naseeb (fortune), the Dimension concept (from a previous session), and pitru-related mechanisms — all begin operating from that point onward. The activation of the space element is the root trigger; everything downstream is then governed by those other , previously-taught mechanisms.
18. Why Consistency in Jaap Matters — With an Important Caveat

Daily jaap (chanting) keeps a person's space-element "portal" continuously open; stopping causes the portal to close and the associated ener gy flow to cease, with physical/practical consequences described colloquially as "band bajegi" (things falling apart). However , Bhaiya is explicit that whether missing even a day or two of practice produces a visible negative consequence depends on one's own individual prarabdh and bhagya — practitioners are cautioned not to take this teaching personally or spiral into anxiety about it, but to treat it purely as knowledge to study .
19. Approach the Subtle World as a Curious Student, Not an Anxious Participant

Bhaiya explicitly recommends treating the sookshm jagat (subtle world) the way a researcher treats a subject of study — with curiosity and detachment — rather than constantly relating every phenomenon back to personal fear or self-blame. Per this teaching, over - personalizing prevents genuine learning; approaching negativity or unusual astral phenomena as something interesting to study , rather than something to panic over , is presented as the healthier and more productive posture.
20. Manifestation as a Space-Element Technique

Repeated visualization/manifestation practice is described as another technique for activating one's own space element: the practitioner keeps the element active and ef fectively waits for a matching external shakti to actualize the intention. This teaching notes candidly that a hoped-for outcome does not always manifest exactly as visualized — but in such cases a dif ferent "way" or path typically opens up instead.
21. The Space Element Does Not Discriminate Positive Fr om Negative

The space element exists within positive and negative phenomena alike — what is positive for one person may be negative for another , and vice versa (illustrated with a stock-market analogy: one trader's profit is necessarily another's loss). The space element itself does not reduce negativity or amplify positivity; per this teaching, it simply equalizes .
22. Continuous 24-Hour Jaap and Gr owing Worldly Influence

Maintaining continuous jaap (even across 24 hours) keeps the portal maximally open, and this teaching states that a person's worldly vircharswa/influence (dabdaba/prabhav) compounds and grows daily as a direct result — precisely because the space element, unlike the other four elements (which are "already accounted for" / fixed), is the one element in which a person can continue writing and expanding their own standing indefinitely .
23. Why Some People Who Left Ashaeiynn Falter ed

Bhaiya notes that people who were previously part of the community and later betrayed or deceived it made, in his assessment, one specific and fatal mistake: they stopped their jaap. He contrasts this with his own and committed sadhaks' continued practice, framing sustained jaap (not physical-world validation) as the true safeguard of standing.
24. Why Bhaiya Says He Only Car es About His Own Space Element

Bhaiya states that everything he has received in the physical world is, in his own account, a byproduct of his space element being active — so his own stated focus, even while sitting among the sangat, is never on physical-world outcomes but purely on maintaining his own space element.
25. A Personal Dhyan Anecdote

Bhaiya shares a light, personal anecdote from that day's own meditation: encountering "Manu Bhaiya" in a vision, a small comedic exchange about wanting to hear a Ram Katha (story of Ram) but being of fered a Shanidev katha first (justified as Shanidev being among the greatest Ram bhakts), and Bhaiya humorously admitting he has since for gotten most of the story's details — jokingly attributing this lapse to married life. This is of fered as a light illustration that the subtle body continues learning new vidyas on an ongoing, evolving basis.
26. Practical Announcement: Dhanteras Hawan on the 18th

Bhaiya closes with a logistical announcement: on the 18th (Dhanteras), an evening hawan will be held specifically for mantra ahuti — participants are encouraged to attend and of fer an ahuti (ritual of fering) of their own personal mantra, so as to strengthen their individual mantra shakti and further awaken their space element. Families are welcome to join, and the event is described as broadly affordable for all.
27. Closing Exhortation: You Asked to Be Her e

Bhaiya's closing message frames each person's presence at Ashaeiynn as the fruit of a past-life prayer for the opportunity to practice bhakti. He states plainly that failing to do jaap or sadhna today makes the practitioner themselves responsible ("doshi") for whatever consequences follow — not anyone else — precisely because they are the one who asked for this opportunity in the first place; by the same logic, whatever joy or reward comes from sustained practice also belongs entirely to the practitioner .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY
God, per this teaching, is defined as: whatever a human being can neither see, hear , nor feel — yet which exists.

Of the five classical elements, only the space element (aakash tatva) meets this definition — earth, water , fire, and air can all be seen or felt directly or through mixing with another element. The space element = God — wherever it mixes into any object, body , or substance, that thing becomes divine. Devotion (bhakti) is one r oute to activating the space element, not the only one — extreme, sustained secular ef fort ("atha mehnat") in any domain can trigger the same activation via a saturation point. "Activation of the space element cr eates miracles" — once triggered, the connection persists and continues to open pathways going forward. Once activated, downstream outcomes are governed by prarabdh, naseeb, the Dimension concept, and pitru mechanisms — the space element is the root trigger , not the whole mechanism. Consistency in jaap keeps the space-element portal open ; stopping closes it — but whether missing practice causes visible harm depends on individual prarabdh/bhagya; never take this personally or anxiously . Approach the subtle world (sookshm jagat) with a student's curiosity , not a fearful, self-r eferential anxiety . The space element does not discriminate positive fr om negative — it equalizes , exactly like markets or any zero-sum system. Continuous jaap compounds worldly influence over time, since the space element (unlike the other four) is the one element in which standing can be indefinitely expanded. Dhanteras (18th) evening hawan will include mantra ahuti — attend and of fer your own mantra's ahuti to strengthen your mantra shakti and space element; families welcome, broadly af fordable. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 51, English)
The Space Element ( आ क ाश त त्व ): Redefining What "God" Actually Is
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. How does Bhaiya define God in this teaching, in the simplest possible terms? A: "Everything that a human being can neither see, hear , nor feel — yet which still exists — is God." This is of fered as the core, simplest working definition arrived at over the course of the session.

Q2. Why doesn't Bhaiya just accept the sangat's initial answers about what God is (energy , consciousness, supr eme power , etc.)? A: Per this teaching, most common definitions collapse under scrutiny — for example, if the universe's "supreme power" alone is God, it's unclear what the rest of the universe would then be; Bhaiya deliberately tests each of fered answer for this kind of internal contradiction before arriving at a cleaner definition.

Q3. Is this the same "inner consciousness" concept about God fr om an earlier Mool Tatva video? A: No — a sangat member raises exactly this earlier framework (inner consciousness/intuition connected to the Kuldevi concept), and Bhaiya explicitly confirms today's teaching is a distinctly dif ferent concept, not a restatement of the earlier one.
Q4. What ar e the five classical elements this teaching is built on? A: Earth, water , fire, air, and space (aakash) — the panchtatva.

Q5. Why ar e earth, water , fire, and air not consider ed "God" under this framework? A: Because, per this teaching, all four can be directly seen or felt — either on their own (heat from fire) or when mixed with another element (air felt as pressure in water , or as soil movement in earth).

Q6. Why specifically is the space element tr eated as God? A: Because it is the one element among the five that can never be seen or felt by ordinary human senses, yet it still exists — meeting the teaching's core definition of God by elimination.

Q7. Does "space element" her e refer to outer space, planets, and stars? A: No — this teaching is explicit that it does not mean literal astronomical space; it refers specifically to the fifth classical element the sages describe as composing the Earth itself, distinct from anything found in the literal cosmos.

Q8. What happens when the space element mixes into an object, body , or substance? A: Per this teaching, that object or substance becomes divine ("bhagwan") — of fered as the underlying mechanism behind practices involving holy water , consecrated food, and murti worship.

Q9. Why do we touch the feet of someone whose subtle chakras ar e open? A: Because, per this teaching, an open subtle chakra system means that person's space element is highly active and connected to the astral world, drawing ener gies from it — treated as being "related to God" in a literal sense.

Q10. Does this framework also explain paranormal entities like ghosts (bhoot-pr et)? A: Yes — this teaching states that any entity capable of an action beyond ordinary human capacity , even a bhoot or pret, gets categorically placed in the "God"/divine category , since it displays the same unseen, unfelt-yet-capable trait that defines the space element.

Q1 1. What does it mean, spiritually , when a person "activates" their own space element? A: Per this teaching, it means literally awakening the very element of God within their own body — not something merely God-like, but the same underlying tatva.

Q12. Does someone need to be devoted or religious to activate their space element? A: No — this teaching's Colonel case study (a soldier who never worships, doesn't consciously invoke God, and still achieves great success) is used specifically to demonstrate that devotion is not a strict requirement.

Q13. If that Colonel never prayed or worshipped, how did he achieve so much? A: Per this teaching, he activated his space element unknowingly through "atha mehnat" (extreme, sustained repeated ef fort — his daily hour -long training runs), which pushed him past a saturation point into complete submersion in the activity , activating his subtle body and, through it, his space element.

Q14. What is the "saturation point" mentioned in this teaching? A: The point reached after enough repetition of any single activity , where a person becomes so completely submer ged that ordinary awareness falls away and muscle memory takes over — the moment at which the subtle body and space element activate.

Q15. Once someone hits this saturation point once, does the activation go away again? A: No — per this teaching, once triggered, the connection persists, and the person continues finding a "way forward" in that domain going forward.

Q16. What's the significance of the phrase "activation of space element cr eates miracles"? A: It summarizes this teaching's core practical claim — that triggering this specific element (through devotion or extreme secular ef fort alike) is what produces seemingly miraculous breakthroughs, answers, or outcomes.

Q17. If bhakti isn't strictly r equired, what r ole does it play in this framework? A: This teaching redefines bhakti as one particular technique or method for accessing the space element — alongside extreme secular ef fort in any domain — rather than the only path available.

Q18. How ar e devi-devata (deities) explained within this space-element framework? A: As powerful, already-activated ener gies belonging to the space element itself, which a devotee can use as accessible aids to enter or connect with that element.

Q19. Once my space element is activated, does everything just work out automatically? A: Not automatically — per this teaching, activation is the root trigger , but what happens afterward is then governed by other previously-taught mechanisms: prarabdh (destiny), naseeb (fortune), the Dimension concept, and pitru-related dynamics.

Q20. What happens if I stop doing my daily jaap? A: Per this teaching, stopping closes the space-element "portal" and the associated ener gy flow ceases, described colloquially as things starting to fall apart ("band bajegi") — though whether missing a day or two produces a visible consequence depends on one's own individual prarabdh and bhagya.

Q21. Should I be anxious if I miss a day of jaap? A: No — Bhaiya is explicit that practitioners should not take this teaching personally or spiral into anxiety about missed practice; it should be approached as knowledge to study , not a source of fear .

Q22. What's the r ecommended mindset for appr oaching the subtle/astral world in general? A: Per this teaching, approach it the way a researcher approaches a subject of study — with curiosity and some detachment — rather than constantly relating every phenomenon back to personal fear or self-blame, since over -personalizing prevents genuine learning.

Q23. Is visualization/manifestation practice connected to this teaching at all? A: Yes — repeated visualization is described as another technique for activating one's space element, where the practitioner keeps the element active while waiting for a matching external shakti to actualize the intention; the exact hoped-for outcome doesn't always manifest, but a dif ferent path typically opens instead.

Q24. Does the space element favor positive outcomes over negative ones? A: No — per this teaching, the space element exists equally within positive and negative phenomena and does not discriminate between them; it simply equalizes, comparable to how one trader's market profit is necessarily another's loss.

Q25. Why does continuous, r ound-the-clock jaap specifically help build worldly influence? A: Because, per this teaching, the space element is the one element (unlike the other four , which are fixed/"already accounted for") in which a person's standing can be indefinitely expanded — so keeping its portal maximally open through continuous jaap compounds that growth daily .

Q26. What mistake does Bhaiya say people who left or betrayed the community made? A: Per this teaching, their specific and fatal mistake was stopping their jaap — contrasted with Bhaiya's and committed sadhaks' continued practice, which he frames as the true safeguard of one's standing, not physical-world validation.

Q27. Why does Bhaiya say he personally focuses only on his own space element rather than physical-world outcomes? A: Because he states everything he has received in the physical world is a byproduct of his space element being active — so maintaining that element, not chasing physical outcomes directly , is his stated priority .

Q28. What is happening on the 18th (Dhanteras), and why should I attend? A: An evening hawan specifically for mantra ahuti — attendees are encouraged to of fer an ahuti of their own personal mantra to strengthen their individual mantra shakti and further awaken their space element; families are welcome, and it is described as broadly af fordable.

Q29. What is Bhaiya's closing message about r esponsibility for one's own practice? A: That each person's presence at Ashaeiynn is the fruit of a past-life prayer for the chance to practice bhakti — so failing to do jaap or sadhna today makes the practitioner themselves responsible for whatever follows, just as any joy or reward from sustained practice also belongs entirely to them.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 51 additions)

Keep the core definition of God ("that which can neither be seen, heard, nor felt, yet exists") tightly scoped to this teaching's own five-element framework — do not present it as a universal or exclusive theological claim. Preserve the distinction between the five elements precisely: earth, water , fire, and air are perceivable (directly or via mixing); only space (aakash) is not — this is the entire basis for the "space element = God" claim. When explaining the army Colonel case study , keep the emphasis on "atha mehnat" (extreme sustained ef fort) and the "saturation point" mechanism, and frame it explicitly as this teaching's own illustrative case study , not a factual claim about any real person. Present bhakti as "one route among several" to activating the space element in this framework, not the exclusive or required path — this session explicitly makes that distinction. When discussing consequences of missing jaap, always include the caveat that outcomes depend on individual prarabdh/bhagya, and explicitly discourage anxious self-blame, consistent with Bhaiya's own stated guidance in this session. Keep the "space element does not discriminate positive from negative, it equalizes" framing intact — avoid implying the space element is a purely benevolent or protective force. Present the Dhanteras/mantra ahuti hawan announcement as time-bound, session-specific logistical information rather than a permanent recurring feature unless later sessions confirm otherwise. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
